request.label: consultants-digest-intro
request.system: You write short, plain, honest prose for a Business Central consultant audience about the Business Central launch event. Use only the facts given. No em-dashes, no bullet lists, no headings, no hype words. Return JSON { "text": "..." } with paragraphs separated by blank lines.
request.prompt:
Write the introduction (3 short paragraphs, 120 to 180 words total) of a "consultant digest" about the 2026 release wave 2 launch event, for Business Central consultants (you implement, configure and train: finance, supply chain, e-documents, sustainability, Expense Agent, reporting, Copilot and the integrations). Tone: direct, a bit of humor, no corporate fluff, no hype adjectives, no em-dashes. Say what themes dominate for this audience and what to watch first. Use only the feature list below; do not add facts. Status rule for this event: a feature is generally available unless the presenters said otherwise; "(implied)" means nothing was said, so treat those as GA and never use the word implied. Do not list features one by one, the list follows your text. Do not use headings.

Features selected for this audience (49, about 134 minutes of video):
- Transfer WIP item and WIP ledger entry (GA (implied), 15 min, Supply chain): A routing line can be marked with a transfer WIP item to track work in progress moved to and from the subcontractor. Posting creates a WIP ledger entry instead of item ledger entries.
- Microsoft Copilot chat in Business Central (GA, 12 min, Copilot and agents): A unified Microsoft Copilot chat opens from the Copilot button in Business Central, replacing the old Copilot UI. It reasons over Business Central data within the user's permissions and context, with progress messages, tables and citations.
- Approval history and audit trail in the web app (announced, 6 min, Expense Agent): The web app shows tabs for draft, submitted, approved and history, and approver tabs. History lists each step with timestamps, approver and rejection reason, and tracks amount changes as part of wider approval improvements.
- Italian Subcontracting Migration app (GA, 6 min, Supply chain): A separate app, not on AppSource, migrates legacy Italian data and is proposed only when needed. It now works in production environments.
- AI policy compliance check (GA (implied), 5 min, Expense Agent): An admin setting lets AI check expenses against policies configured per expense category, and flag non-compliant or unclear items for the approver. It can use Copilot credits.
- Web and general knowledge answers (GA (implied), 4 min, Copilot and agents): Copilot answers questions not tied to Business Central data using the internet and documentation, such as sales tax setup or travel directions. It can also combine Business Central data with web data, like converting item prices with a web exchange rate.
- EDI in Business Central (GA (implied), 4 min, E-Documents): EDI is added to exchange order information between buyer and seller instead of sending email. It is built on the existing E-Documents technology and the PEPPOL format, with a log for each exchange.
- Return documents for Shopify refunds and exchanges (GA (implied), 4 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Refunds can create a sales return order or credit memo, chosen in the return and refund processing setting, using the same parameters as the sales order. For exchanges, Move Negative Lines creates a sales order or invoice for the exchange line.
- Report themes and header footer layouts (GA (implied), 4 min, Reporting and analytics): Branding such as colors and fonts, and header and footer content, is defined once as a theme or header footer layout and reused across document reports. The demo shows one customer statement body layout combined with different themes and header footers.
- Subcontracting comments and attachments (GA (implied), 4 min, Supply chain): Routing lines get a subcontracting comment copied to the purchase order, editable or inherited from standard tasks. Routing attachments have toggles to flow to the production order and purchase lines, so the supplier gets instructions.
- Withholding tax for employees (GA (implied), 3 min, Finance): Withholding tax, previously available for vendors, is extended to employees with new fields for employee rules. Posting an expense report above the threshold creates withholding tax entries, and it can also be used in the general journal.
- Tax rate mismatch handling (preview (implied), 3 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): If the Business Central tax rate differs from the Shopify rate, the order is not created and a review is forced. The user keeps the Business Central rate or overrides it with the Shopify rate.
- VAT reclaim on expense reports (GA (implied), 3 min, Expense Agent): VAT details from receipts build a VAT specification per line, with multiple rates. Posting uses normal VAT posting groups and creates GL and VAT entries for accountant review.
- Inventory put-away for subcontracting (GA (implied), 3 min, Supply chain): Subcontracted items can be received with inventory put-aways on locations requiring put-away and pick. Serial numbers flow into put-away lines and quantity to handle can be auto filled.
- Withholding tax on expense report posting (GA (implied), 3 min, Expense Agent): An expense above the threshold produces a withholding tax entry on posting, visible in preview posting.
- Subcontractor prices with closest match (GA (implied), 3 min, Supply chain): Subcontractor prices are matched by closest match on quantity, date, task, unit of measure and variant, not lowest price. A larger order can get a higher unit price.
- System fields in analysis mode (GA (implied), 3 min, Reporting and analytics): System fields such as created by, created on, modified by and modified on are always available in the analysis mode column picker. This works even if the list page does not show them.
- B2B catalog import and duplicates (GA (implied), 3 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): B2B catalogs are imported only when the company exists in Business Central. Price sync is prevented for catalogs linked to two company locations.
- Use Shopify order number (GA (implied), 3 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): A setting in order synchronization on the Shopify shop card lets sales orders and invoices use the Shopify order number as document number with a Shopify number series. The setting is inherited when an order is imported.
- Bookmark views to role center (announced, 3 min, Reporting and analytics): A bookmark view action on analysis views and saved list views puts the view on the role center. It suits views used as mini reports.
- Travel requests (announced, 3 min, Expense Agent): Employees request permission to spend with budget, dates and justification, and the company sees expected expenses. On approval an expense report per trip follows and receipts are assigned to it.
- Layout status for app-supplied layouts (GA (implied), 3 min, Reporting and analytics): A Layout status menu on the report layouts page lets an administrator set a lifecycle state such as draft, pending approval, approved or retired on app-supplied layouts, including Microsoft ones. Layouts that are not approved do not show on the request page and only appear on the report layout page.
- Legacy subcontracting pre-check (GA (implied), 3 min, Supply chain): An action checks for open transfer and purchase orders with WIP items before disabling legacy subcontracting. The same checks run on disable.
- Direct transfer modes (GA (implied), 3 min, Supply chain): Direct transfer can post in one go or create separate shipment and receipt documents. Ship and receipt mode supports partial shipping and warehouse shipment.
- Tax area code and tax liable on Shopify orders and refunds (preview, 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Shopify orders get tax area code and tax liable fields, filled from Shopify or by AI and used when the sales document is created, and they can be overridden to skip standard mapping. The Shopify refund page gets a tax fact box and tax lines.
- Auto create B2B catalog (GA (implied), 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): The toggle creates a catalog linked to the company location so Business Central prices apply. Market catalogs are an alternative for simpler plans.
- Subcontracting purchase order lines (GA (implied), 2 min, Supply chain): The generated purchase order holds lines for vendor-supplied components, the routing operation, an info line and comment lines with instructions.
- Item charges on subcontracting receipts (GA (implied), 2 min, Supply chain): Item charges can be assigned to posted subcontracting receipt lines, including the operation line. Production order statistics show the charge in subcontractor cost.
- Install Subcontracting app from Manufacturing Setup (GA (implied), 2 min, Supply chain): The app can be installed from Manufacturing Setup when disabling legacy subcontracting. Without legacy data no migration runs.
- Released production orders from planning worksheet (GA (implied), 2 min, Supply chain): Carrying out action messages can create production orders as released, or released and print. Flushing posts consumption and capacity on creation.
- Cross-environment master data management (GA (implied), 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Subsidiaries in other environments of the same tenant can pull master data from the HQ company. It is built in, with no middleware or custom code, and uses the same UI as same-environment synchronization.
- Flagged and compliant policy statuses (GA (implied), 2 min, Expense Agent): Reports and lines show compliant or flagged, with AI reasoning beside flagged expenses. Missing receipt info also flags a line.
- Expense Agent mobile app (preview, 2 min, Expense Agent): A new mobile app for iOS and Android scans receipts, crops the background and works offline. Users accept beta conditions and need a Business Central environment that supports the Expense Agent.
- Company tax registration ID and country extensions (GA, 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Tax registration IDs are now populated when creating customers. Small Belgium and US extensions are added, and Belgium adds an Enterprise number option.
- Subcontracting with warehouse receipt (GA, 2 min, Supply chain): For directed put-away locations, a subcontracting order needs a warehouse receipt. Put-away with serial numbers is created only for the last operation, otherwise output is registered.
- Review and approve tax match (preview (implied), 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): A review window shows the tax area, jurisdictions and taxes per shipping and product line. A red icon marks low confidence and the user approves or cancels.
- Power BI apps on Fabric (announced, 2 min, Reporting and analytics): The Power BI apps were converted to the Fabric backend. They will come as samples or on AppSource in single- and multi-company versions.
- Subcontracting details fact box on routing (GA (implied), 2 min, Supply chain): A fact box on production order routing shows whether a line is subcontracted, connected components and the WIP quantity at the subcontractor. It drills down to WIP ledger entries and links purchase, transfer and production orders.
- Presubmission policy check (GA (implied), 2 min, Expense Agent): Submitters can run the AI policy check manually with a check policies button before sending the report. It is not automatic for submitters and can be turned off to save AI credits.
- Business Central data questions (GA (implied), 2 min, Copilot and agents): Copilot searches Business Central data with the user's context, permissions and company, for example most urgent sales orders. It also analyzes sales data, such as the least sold items, and suggests actions.
- Follow-up conversation and suggestions (GA (implied), 2 min, Copilot and agents): Users keep asking in the same conversation and Copilot suggests follow-up questions. Responses are grounded and can include charts and tables.
- E-document messages (GA (implied), 2 min, E-Documents): A message architecture attaches messages such as acknowledgement and order response to the e-document. These messages are linked to the original document.
- Sample layouts for themes (GA (implied), 2 min, Reporting and analytics): The Word add-in has sample documents to preview style, font and color changes. You then save, clear the content and upload as a theme.
- Composite layout menu on a body layout (GA (implied), 2 min, Reporting and analytics): On a body layout in the report layouts page, a composite layout menu lets you pick the theme and header footer for testing. Running the report then shows the chosen combination.
- Export logs pushed to Fabric (preview, 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Synchronization logs are also written into Fabric for monitoring through the SQL endpoint.
- Mileage rates per period (GA (implied), 2 min, Expense Agent): Mileage allowance can have start and end dates for several periods. The rate is picked based on the expense date.
- Multi-company Power BI reporting (announced, 2 min, Reporting and analytics): Multi-company app versions show data across companies with a company filter.
- Invoicing for France (GA, 2 min, E-Documents): Invoicing for France is introduced with three new e-document formats set up on the e-document service, including e-reporting. Lifecycle events such as collected, submitted, accepted, refused and technical rejected are stored as messages linked to the invoice e-document.
- Citations, progress messages and sources (GA (implied), 2 min, Copilot and agents): Answers include clickable citation pills, progress messages and a sources button listing what the AI used.

output.text:
Subcontracting is the loudest theme here. A new Subcontracting app, WIP ledger entries, purchase order lines, put-aways and a migration path for legacy data take up a big share of the supply chain time. If you have clients on the legacy setup, start there, because disabling it comes with a pre-check and, for Italian data, a separate migration app that now works in production.

Next in line are the Expense Agent and the new Microsoft Copilot chat, which replaces the old Copilot UI. Expect questions about AI policy checks, VAT reclaim, withholding tax and credits, and expect users to ask Copilot about everything, including things unrelated to their data. Reporting gets themes and header footer layouts, and e-documents get EDI and invoicing for France.

Treat the Shopify tax features carefully. Tax matching is in preview, as are the Expense Agent mobile app and the Fabric export logs. Several items are only announced, such as travel requests and the Power BI apps on Fabric, so keep them out of project plans.
